source: If the promise is binding, breaking it is wrong. The promise is not binding. Thus breaking it is not wrong.

reconstruction.title: Argument about the binding nature of a promise

claims.text: If the promise is binding, breaking it is wrong.

formalization.domain_description: The domain consists of truth values (true/false) for propositional statements about promises and moral status.

translations.reason: Direct translation of the conditional statement 'If P then Q'

interpretation_notes: The argument uses propositional logic with P representing the binding nature of the promise and Q representing the moral status of breaking it
The logical form follows the structure: (P → Q), ¬P ⊢ ¬Q
This translation preserves the surface-level logical structure without evaluating its validity (which would be an instance of the fallacy of denying the antecedent)
